units.text: INT. ROADSIDE WAY STATION - DAY
Adobe walls, a stove gone cold, six mismatched chairs pulled to a long table.
Dust hangs in the shaft of light from the door.
Outside, a horse stamps.
Six people sit down to a meal none of them wants.
The proprietor, MA TULLIVER, sixty, sleeves rolled, ladles beans into tin bowls and says nothing.
Her hired boy, SPARROW, fifteen, sets them down one by one.
A drummer in a checked vest, ORVILLE PENN, forty, sits with his sample case under his boots.
A woman in gray travel wool, SABINA ROJAS, thirty, holds her bowl and does not lift the spoon.
A tall rancher, OSCAR HALE, fifty, takes his hat off for grace though no one says one.
And in the corner chair, back to the wall, a stranger in a dusty duster, JUDE CALLAHAN, thirty-five, watches the door.
The beans steam.
For a long moment there is only the sound of spoons.
Lovely weather for the road.
units.name: ORVILLE

units.text: It's rained twice in a year.
units.name: OSCAR

units.text: That's what I said.
units.name: ORVILLE

units.text: Is there a stage tonight?
units.name: SABINA

units.text: Stage came and went.
units.name: MA TULLIVER

units.text: I was told it comes at four.
units.name: SABINA

units.text: It did come at four. You were upstairs.
units.name: SPARROW

units.text: Nobody woke me.
units.name: SABINA

units.text: Sparrow, fetch the bread.
units.name: MA TULLIVER

units.text: He goes.
Oscar glances at Jude, who has not touched his bowl.
Orville clears his throat and opens his mouth, but Sabina speaks first.
Mister, are you not hungry?
units.name: SABINA

units.text: Not particularly.
units.name: JUDE

units.text: He's waiting on somebody.
units.name: OSCAR

units.text: I'm waiting on supper to finish.
units.name: JUDE

units.text: Then it's finished.
units.name: OSCAR

units.text: He shoves his bowl away.
Ma Tulliver sets down her ladle.
The room tightens like a drawn cord.
She comes around the table, slow, wiping her hands on her apron.
She stops behind Jude's chair and rests one palm on its back.
He does not turn his head.
Sparrow returns with the bread, sees them, and stops in the doorway with the loaf held against his chest.
Ma?
units.name: SPARROW

units.text: Put it down, son.
units.name: MA TULLIVER

units.text: He sets it on the sideboard.
Orville slides his sample case farther under his chair.
Sabina rises halfway, then sits again as Oscar lays a hand over hers.
Ma'am. You know who I am.
units.name: JUDE

units.text: I know whose boy you are.
units.name: MA TULLIVER

units.text: We all know whose boy.
units.name: ^OSCAR

units.text: Jude smiles, tired.
He reaches into his duster.
Everyone in the room draws a breath, and what he takes out is a folded letter, creased soft with handling.
He asked me to bring this.
units.name: JUDE

units.text: He sets it on the table, in the middle of the beans.
Nobody reaches for it.
Outside the horse stamps, and stamps again, and a long shadow crosses the doorway.
